entries.note: 'Bad news' evaluates the development without specifying a factual outcome.

entries.test: Public revenue disclosures, customer spending records, and details of SpaceX's contribution would establish whether tokenmaxxing substantially contributed to Anthropic's quarter.
entries.note: The SpaceX subsidy is asserted as background, not stated as a condition.

entries.test: Provider revenue disclosures and enterprise spending records would show whether tokenmaxxing generated substantial short-term revenue for Anthropic and OpenAI.
entries.note: The revenue assertion is causal and checkable. The normalization strengthens 'never seemed like a sustainable idea to me' into categorical unsustainability.
This is Marcus's own embedded post, expressing a judgment about the practice.
'May have' and 'looks like' preserve uncertainty about both the revenue contribution and the trend's durability.

entries.test: Public customer accounts and responses to accidental monthly consumption of roughly half a billion tokens would show whether customers accept such incidents comfortably.
entries.note: The normalization narrows 'nobody' to enterprise customers and turns an incident in one month into a monthly formulation.

entries.test: Enterprise AI budget disclosures and spending surveys would show whether companies tighten AI budgets after the post.
entries.note: 'Especially when' emphasizes a driver; it does not make the forecast contingent on that driver.

entries.test: Public measurements comparing agent workflows with ordinary non-agent AI use would establish token-consumption ratios and associated costs.
entries.note: Ordinary non-agent use is the natural implied comparison.

entries.test: Public enterprise usage data and provider financial disclosures would show whether retreat from tokenmaxxing reduces revenue or lowers prices and worsens profitability.
entries.note: Marcus presents a consequence of a reported ongoing retreat. The normalization recasts it as hypothetical and adds that providers 'will have to' cut prices.

entries.test: Dated public posts and reporting would show whether reports of enterprise token spending without significant ROI were increasingly appearing around publication.
entries.note: 'I am seeing more' is narrower than asserting an overall increase in the number of reports.
The quoted sentence belongs to another author; the possibility that it becomes an era's epitaph is Marcus's own assertion.
The source says 'could' and treats the cited projections conditionally. The normalization makes already-negative Big Tech ROI an established premise.

entries.test: Government announcements and enacted financial rescue measures would establish whether AI-industry bailouts occur.
entries.note: 'Brace for bailouts' plainly predicts bailouts without a deadline. The normalization adds a probability hedge and a specific causal explanation.
